name: Nikolay Petrushev
strengths: Petrushev slides back in pass protection and uses that 6-6 reach so the rusher has to go the long way.
Petrushev locks on in the run game, drives the defensive tackle inside, then gets up and walls off the linebacker.
Petrushev has 6-6 length that works better once he sits in his stance and plays from a lower pad.
weaknesses: Petrushev plays too high and bends at the waist. The next step is sitting in his stance so that length works from a lower pad.
comparison: Petrushev comps to Wyatt Milum — same 6-6 frame, long arms, still filling out toward starter weight.
projection: Petrushev should spend Year 1 getting bigger, then rotate in Year 2 and 3. Ceiling is a multi-year SEC starter if the weight comes and he plays lower.
schemeFit: Petrushev fits as a tackle who wins with length first while the weight catches up and he learns to play lower.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-10-06 from Hudl sophomore reel (embed 22939035 / 696521776d1a93cef5fc9037), East Lake. Do not assign pad-level work as Trautwein's first job — tape only. Comp size-matched within ~1–2 inches — not a Florida-alum default.
insiderNotes: Petrushev is a 6-6 / 285 East Lake tackle who slides back and uses his length so rushers have to go the long way, then locks on and gets up to the linebacker on runs. He plays too high. The next step is sitting in his stance. Florida offered June 1; Trautwein; two unofficials, latest Sept. 5.

angle: Lead with East Lake 6-6 length + Florida offer heat after FNL.
